title_en: Mining for tourists in China
abstract_en: A digital ethnography of mining-heritage tourism in China. Relevant because it offers an empirical model for industrial-heritage regeneration — extending to the Grand Canal's industrial sections and abandoned-port assessments. J. Heritage Tourism 19(1) (2024); some bibliographies cite 2023, 2024 issue used here.
tags: heritage tourism, industrial heritage, digital ethnography, China

title_en: Conflict over the 2024 Bothnian herring quota
abstract_en: Narrative policy analysis of the Bothnian herring quota conflict in Sociologia Ruralis. Background to Gotland's fisheries disputes and a direct case for the food-corridor framework on Gotland. Wiley lists M. B. Gillette as sole author.
tags: herring, fisheries, Gotland, narrative policy analysis, food corridor

title_en: Imagining for Real
abstract_en: Ingold's essay on creation, attention and correspondence — the futures-literacy counterpart to the project's regeneration framing. Treated here as Routledge 2022 / openedition 2021.
tags: attention, correspondence, creation, futures literacy

title_en: Lines: A Brief History
abstract_en: Wayfaring versus transport: culture is made along the lines people move through the world. The theoretical core of the corridor-as-living-line idea — 'follow the movement, not the monument' — grounding the three-walk method used on the Beijing canal and in Gotland.
tags: wayfaring, walking, lines, movement, corridor theory

title_en: In Defense of Things: Archaeology and the Ontology of Objects
abstract_en: The ontological standing of things — ruins, boats, porcelain act back on people. Basis of the 'follow one thing' method and of treating canal locks, grindstones and decommissioned harbours as agents rather than background.
tags: materiality, things, ontology, archaeology

title_en: Ruin Memories: Materialities, Aesthetics and the Archaeology of the Recent Past
abstract_en: How to treat modern ruins and leftovers: the keep-the-ruin argument for canal leftovers and abandoned Gotland fishing harbours — care and attention rather than demolition or faithful restoration.
tags: ruins, memory, materiality, recent past

title_en: Curated Decay: Heritage Beyond Saving
abstract_en: Care without rescue: heritage does not have to be saved to have value. Supports assessing what to keep, let decay, or let transform at decommissioned infrastructure along the corridor.
tags: curated decay, care, transformation, heritage

title_en: Heritage Futures: Comparative Approaches to Natural and Cultural Heritage Practices
abstract_en: Umbrella statement of the heritage-futures research programme — uncertainty, transformation, profusion, diversity. Frames the project's regeneration agenda and the treatment of the past as a resource for viable futures. UCL Press, open access.
authors: Rodney Harrison, Caitlin DeSilvey, Cornelius Holtorf, Sharon Macdonald et al.
tags: heritage futures, transformation, uncertainty, profusion

title_en: Memorylands: Heritage and Identity in Europe Today
abstract_en: Memory, identity and heritage in Europe — 'memoryscapes' and difficult heritage as background for the comparative reading of Gotland and the Beijing canal societies.
tags: memory, difficult heritage, Europe, identity

title_en: Uses of Heritage
abstract_en: Heritage is not a thing but a cultural process, and the 'Authorised Heritage Discourse' (AHD) naturalises elite Western values. Keeps the project alert to power in heritage-making and tourism claims. Routledge.
tags: critical heritage, AHD, cultural process, authorised heritage discourse

title_en: Discussing strategy in heritage conservation: living heritage approach as an example of strategic innovation
abstract_en: The living heritage approach reframed as a strategic innovation: community continuity at the centre of conservation. The theoretical base of the project's 'living/lived heritage' claims and community engagement. J. Cultural Heritage Management and Sustainable Development 4(1): 16-34.
tags: living heritage, strategy, community, conservation

title_en: The Past in the Present: A Living Heritage Approach — Meteora, Greece
abstract_en: Open-access monograph developing the living heritage approach with the Meteora case — communities and sites as one inseparable entity. Ubiquity Press.
tags: living heritage, Meteora, authenticity, community

title_en: People-Centred Approaches to the Conservation of Cultural Heritage: Living Heritage
abstract_en: ICCROM guidance on people-centred approaches: continuity of use, community capacities, co-management. The institutional anchor for the project's community work. Rome: ICCROM.
tags: people-centred, living heritage, ICCROM, co-management

title_en: The making of the Grand Canal in China: beyond knowledge and power
abstract_en: Actor-network account of the 2014 Grand Canal nomination: heritage as the negotiated product of human and non-human agencies — beyond simple statements of state power. International Journal of Heritage Studies 27(6): 584-600.
tags: Grand Canal, actor-network, nomination, heritage making

title_en: The Grand Canal as World Heritage: living heritage in the 21st century?
abstract_en: Sheffield PhD: a critical reading that the canal's heritagisation has often functioned as development, while little original fabric remains. White Rose eTheses 20989 (submitted 2018-03).
tags: Grand Canal, critical heritage, living heritage, urban development

title_en: Population, wars and the Grand Canal in Chinese history
abstract_en: Quantitative long-run evidence linking population, wars and the Grand Canal through Chinese history — background for the canal's demographic and political-integrative role. Sustainability 14: 7006.
authors: H. F. Lee, X. Jia, B. Ji
tags: Grand Canal, population, war, long-run history

title_en: Spatial distribution and pedigree age of intangible cultural heritage along the Grand Canal
abstract_en: Maps the living folk-song/chant/event landscape along the canal (e.g. boatmen's chants) as a corridor-wide phenomenon. Heritage Science 12: 246.
authors: S. Zhang, X. Zhang, J. Liu
tags: intangible heritage, Grand Canal, folk songs, spatial analysis

title_en: 'Authenticity' as a pathway to sustainable cultural tourism?
abstract_en: Gotland and Rapa Nui compared — the direct evidence for testing the project's 'living' versus 'authentic' tourism claims. Sustainability 13(11): 6302.
authors: G. Poort, U. Persson-Fischier, Helene Martinsson-Wallin, J. Elf Donaldson, M. Schaub
tags: authenticity, cultural tourism, Gotland, Rapa Nui, sustainability

title_en: Under storkökets golv. Arkeologisk undersökning i Gamla Skogsby 2021
abstract_en: Excavation report of the 2021 season at the Iron Age village of Gamla Skogsby, Southern Öland — kitchen and feasting evidence (pig bones, pottery, grindstones) anchoring the regeneration fieldwork. The same volume (Kalmar Studies in Archaeology XIV) hosts Holtorf 2022, pp. 85-123. Linnaeus University.
tags: Gamla Skogsby, excavation, Iron Age, feast, Southern Öland

title_en: An Archaeology of Growth and Regeneration
abstract_en: The programmatic chapter reading the Gamla Skogsby soil and food evidence as the past generating future life. In Under storkökets golv, Kalmar Studies in Archaeology XIV, pp. 85-123.
tags: growth, regeneration, heritage futures, Gamla Skogsby

title_en: Sweetness and Power: The Place of Sugar in Modern History
abstract_en: The modern history of a single commodity (sugar) as the tracer of capitalism and culture — the intellectual model behind the project's food-tracing method (porridge, herring, tribute grain). Viking.
tags: food anthropology, commodity, taste, capitalism

title_en: China's Porcelain Capital: The Rise, Fall and Reinvention of Ceramics in Jingdezhen
abstract_en: A working model for how a place rises, declines and rebrands through heritage — directly comparable to Beijing's canal landscape and Gotland's fishing heritage. Bloomsbury.
tags: Jingdezhen, porcelain, heritagisation, reinvention

title_en: Copying, Counterfeiting, and Capitalism in Contemporary China: Jingdezhen's Porcelain Industry
abstract_en: The authenticity-versus-replication question that runs beneath canal heritagisation and heritage tourism. Modern China 36(4): 367-403.
tags: copying, counterfeiting, authenticity, China, material production

title_en: Baltic Prehistoric Interactions and Transformations: The Neolithic to the Iron Age
abstract_en: Gotland within regional corridor networks of the Neolithic-Iron Age — conversing with Beijing as a convergence node of the canal-Silk Roads interface, and providing the islands-comparison baseline. Gotland University Press.
tags: Baltic, prehistory, networks, Gotland, connectivity

title_en: Ceramics and Society: A Technological Approach to Archaeological Assemblages
abstract_en: The summa of the French chaîne opératoire school: decoding ceramic assemblages as coalitions of technical choices whose boundaries are social boundaries. Directly operational for the Grand Canal's kiln and craft corridors — Gillette's Jingdezhen porcelain material can be re-read through it: transmission is never diffusion but learning along network boundaries. Roux & Courty, Springer 2019 (English translation of Des Céramiques et des Hommes).
tags: chaîne opératoire, ceramics, technical choices, social boundaries, transmission

title_en: Persisting technological boundaries: Social interactions, cognitive correlations and polarization
abstract_en: Ethnoarchaeological and modelling evidence (potters in India and Africa) that technological boundaries persist where social interaction is endogamous and learning is bounded — a mechanism account of why crafts travel along some corridors and stop at others. Roux, Bril, Cauliez, Goujon, Lara, Manen, de Saulieu & Zangato, Journal of Anthropological Archaeology 48: 320–335.
authors: Valentine Roux, B. Bril, J. Cauliez, A.-L. Goujon, C. Lara, C. Manen, G. de Saulieu, E. Zangato
tags: technological boundaries, learning, social networks, ethnoarchaeology, polarization

title_en: Chaîne Opératoire, technological networks and sociological interpretations
abstract_en: Programmatic statement: the chaîne opératoire, formalised as technological networks, is a tool for modelling the relational structure of societies — linking micro-sequences of technical choices to macro patterns of interaction. Methodological backbone for reading corridor craft complexes. Cuadernos de Prehistoria y Arqueología de la Universidad de Granada 30, special issue 'Social ceramics'.
tags: chaîne opératoire, technological networks, modelling, sociological interpretation

title_en: The Impact of Buddhism on Chinese Material Culture
abstract_en: The first systematic account of how Buddhism reshaped China's everyday material world: relics, prayer beads and monastic clothing, and apparently secular things such as the bridge, tea and the chair. For this project the bridge is the master-figure of the corridor — the canal is a chain of bridges — and incense, tea and the bowl travel along it, carrying religious practice into ordinary meals and daily exchange. Princeton University Press, 2003.
tags: material culture, Buddhism, everyday objects, bridges, tea

title_en: Religion and Material Culture: The Matter of Belief
abstract_en: David Morgan's edited volume treats belief as embodied, material practice rather than creedal assent — objects, images, spaces and performance as the medium of devotion. Naming credential for the everyday-texture framing of this dimension: faith is read through the incense-burner, the porridge pot and the market-day offering, not through doctrine. Routledge, 2010.
tags: material religion, embodied belief, matter of belief, practice

title_en: Inscriptions of Beijing Inner-City Temples: A Social-History Survey (Vol. 6)
abstract_en: Franco-Chinese field project (École française d'Extrême-Orient with Beijing Normal University) surveying temples inside the Beijing city walls on the grid of the Qianlong 'Full City Map': stele texts transcribed, temple gazetteers written, incised and annotated, with indices of incense-fair societies (香会). Primary epigraphic ground-truth for Beijing's everyday-belief texture beneath Shichahai and the canal-side temple belt. National Library of China Publishing House, 2024.
authors: 谢玲琼 (Xie Lingqiong, comp.); 吕敏 (Marianne Bujard, gen. ed.)
tags: Beijing temples, stele inscriptions, incense fairs, social history

title_en: Miaofengshan Temple Fair — National Intangible Cultural Heritage (X-84)
abstract_en: Register entry (2008, second national batch, category 民俗/folklore) for the Miaofengshan temple fair: spring incense (lunar 4/1–4/15) and autumn (7/25–8/1) pilgrimages service by incense-fair societies (香会) and tea sheds along the road — the living organizational texture of a Beijing-hinterland festival cult. China Intangible Cultural Heritage website (ihchina).
authors: 中国非物质文化遗产网 (ihchina register)
tags: temple fair, Miaofengshan, intangible heritage, pilgrimage

title_en: Miaofengshan (妙峰山)
abstract_en: Field monograph of the 1925 survey — the first folklore fieldwork in Chinese academic history — led by Gu Jiegang under Peking University's Institute of Chinese Studies: how pilgrims walked to the summit, the tea sheds and incense societies that fed them, and the everyday order of a climb the city did as excursion. Sun Yat-sen (Zhongshan) University, 1928.
tags: folklore, field survey, Miaofengshan, tea sheds, 1925

title_en: Carnival and the Everyday: Temple Fairs and Popular Culture in Ming–Qing China (狂欢与日常：明清时期的庙会与民间文化)
abstract_en: Shiyu Zhao's classic argument that the 'carnival spirit' of temple fairs is continuous with, not an escape from, daily life — fairs as routine, sociable and inclusive popular culture. The methodological hinge for reading Beijing's fair-economy and belief-as-texture rather than belief-as-doctrine. SDX (Sanlian) Press, 2002.
tags: temple fairs, carnival, popular culture, Ming-Qing, daily life

title_en: Above and Along the Great River: Northern Chinese Urban-Rural Life since the Tenth Century (大河上下：10世纪以来的北方城乡与民众生活)
abstract_en: A regional social history across the northern corridor — city and countryside, official and popular — by one of the project's key methodologists; grounds the canal's northern everyday in ten centuries of household, market and belief practice. Shanxi People's Publishing House, 2010.
tags: regional social history, northern China, everyday life, households

title_en: Religion in Chinese Society: A Study of Contemporary Social Functions of Religion and Some of Their Historical Factors
abstract_en: C. K. Yang's distinction between institutional and 'diffused' religion: Chinese religion penetrates daily life — kinship, markets, guilds, festivals — without an autonomous institutional shell. The theoretical charter for reading belief as a texture of ordinary exchange along the canal rather than as a separate sacred sphere. University of California Press, 1961.
tags: diffused religion, Chinese society, institutional religion, festivals

title_en: Popular Religion in China: The Imperial Metaphor
abstract_en: Fieldwork-grounded account (People's Republic and Taiwan) of local cults, incense-burners and festivals as shared social imagination — popular religion as the 'poetry of collective vision' enacted in temple, image and festival, irreducible to any named religion. Routledge, 2001 (orig. 1992), Routledge Revivals 2021.
tags: popular religion, imperial metaphor, local cults, incense-burner, festivals
